{{Short description|Mathematical subcategories of Grothendieck categories}}
In mathematics, '''Giraud subcategories''' form an important class of subcategories of [[Grothendieck category|Grothendieck categories]]. They are named after [[Jean Giraud (mathematician)|Jean Giraud]].

== Definition ==

Let <math>\mathcal{A}</math> be a [[Grothendieck category]]. A full subcategory <math>\mathcal{B}</math> is called ''reflective'', if the inclusion functor <math>i\colon\mathcal{B}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}</math> has a [[adjoint functors|left adjoint]]. If this left adjoint of <math>i</math> also preserves 
[[kernel (category theory)|kernels]], then <math>\mathcal{B}</math> is called a ''Giraud subcategory''.

== Properties ==
Let <math>\mathcal{B}</math> be Giraud in the Grothendieck category <math>\mathcal{A}</math> and <math>i\colon\mathcal{B}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}</math> the inclusion functor.
* <math>\mathcal{B}</math> is again a Grothendieck category.
* An object <math>X</math> in <math>\mathcal{B}</math> is [[injective object|injective]] if and only if <math>i(X)</math> is injective in <math>\mathcal{A}</math>.
* The left adjoint <math>a\colon\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{B}</math> of <math>i</math> is [[exact functor|exact]].
* Let <math>\mathcal{C}</math> be a [[localizing subcategory]] of <math>\mathcal{A}</math> and <math>\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C}</math> be the associated [[Quotient of an abelian category|quotient category]]. The section functor <math>S\colon\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}</math> is [[full and faithful functors|fully faithful]] and induces an [[equivalence of categories|equivalence]] between <math>\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C}</math> and the Giraud subcategory <math>\mathcal{B}</math> given by the  <math>\mathcal{C}</math>-closed objects in <math>\mathcal{A}</math>.
